# v0.9.12 - A Backup You Can Prove Restores, and a Run a Script Can Read

## What's Changed in v0.9.12

A backup can now be proven restorable, a scheduled run can report in a form a script reads, and every long phase says how much is left. Nothing about what is stored changes, and no run's exit code changes unless `--exit-warnings` is passed.

### Added
- **`--restore-drill [N|all]`.** Restores the newest snapshot (or `--ref`) into a temporary directory, checks every file byte-for-byte, runs `git fsck`, downloads N randomly chosen payload files (default 10) and compares their SHA-256, then deletes the directory. A failed drill keeps the directory and names it. It needs the disk for the whole vault; set `TMP` or `TMPDIR` to use a bigger volume.
- **`--json`.** One JSON document on stdout (`schema`, `mode`, `status` of `ok`/`warnings`/`failed`, `exit_code`, `seconds`, `warnings`, `error`, `result`); the human text moves to stderr. The keys of a mode are only ever added to.
- **`--exit-warnings`.** Exit `3` instead of `0` when a run completed but printed a `Warning:`. Off by default, so a scheduled job that works today does not start failing. The exit codes are documented in SNAPSHOT.md and USER_GUIDE.
- **Progress with a rate and a time left for hashing, a payload restore and `--payload-verify`,** the line an upload already printed: `progress: 41.2 GiB of 292.0 GiB hashed (14%), 52 MiB/s, about 1h20m left`. The estimate counts only the files that really are read, not those the hash cache vouches for.

### Fixed
- **A hashing pass that was killed lost everything it had hashed.** The hash cache was saved only when hashing finished or an upload then failed, so a kill, a crash or a power cut at 90% of a 131 GiB tree read it all again. The cache is now saved about once a minute while hashing, under the same trust rule (size, mtime, inode, ctime and device must still match).

### Upgrading

Nothing about what is stored changes and no setting is renamed. A run's exit code is what it was; `--exit-warnings` (which adds `3`) is opt-in. Hashing, a payload restore and `--payload-verify` print a `progress:` line once a minute, as an upload does, which a script reading their output will see.

The full list is in `CHANGELOG.md`.
